assumptions: The handout gives no number for 'quickly', so the LED must change within 100 ms of the first press edge, which is about where people start to notice a delay.
A bouncy press is 5 edges 200 us apart, ending LOW (pressed).
Releasing the button is the board letting go of D2, so the student's INPUT_PULLUP pulls it high.
Serial lines may end with \n or \r\n.
Releasing the button must not toggle the LED (only presses do).

checks.requirement: The first bouncy press turns the LED on exactly once, within 100 ms.
checks.feedback: In loop(), the toggle only executes when the debounced level becomes HIGH (line 27: `if (stable == HIGH)`). Since BTN_PIN uses INPUT_PULLUP and the button is active-low, HIGH is the *released* state, not the pressed one - so the LED and the print happen one step late, on release instead of on press. That is why no LED edge or ON print is seen while the button is held down (press1), but the toggle instead shows up when the button comes back up.

checks.requirement: The first press prints ON on its own line on Serial1.
checks.feedback: Same root cause: the `Serial1.println(on ? "ON" : "OFF")` call is inside the same `if (stable == HIGH)` block, so it only runs on release, producing no text during the press window.

checks.requirement: The first press prints ON on its own line on Serial1.
